paragraphs: Cyvl sells a sensor and software platform that shows cities what needs attention across every street, sidewalk and asset. Counties are a second audience, using it to keep sprawling road networks current.

A city team mounts the LiDAR and 360 degree imaging rig on a vehicle it already owns, and the drive itself does the collecting. Each drive becomes pavement scores, asset inventories and a ranked list of needs. The results live in one shared platform for public works, city leaders and residents. Coverage reaches past pavement to sidewalks and curb ramps assessed for an ADA baseline.

Cities and towns are described as capturing their entire right-of-way in a single pass. Counties are described as using the record to hold developers and utilities accountable for the condition they leave roads in. The company says Atlanta moved downtown pavement from 64 to 75, from fair to good, while potholes fell 60 percent.

quote.text: Scan the network, turn current conditions into a plan, show what changed, then repeat so the city’s picture never goes stale.
